Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import json
def f(g):
    import collections
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for r_ in g for x in r_)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # find frames: colors appearing as solid rectangles
    colors=[c for c in cnt if c!=bg]
    # innermost = color with smallest bbox; frames ordered by size
    def bbox(c):
        rs=[i for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        cs=[j for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        return min(rs),min(cs),max(rs),max(cs)
    info={}
    for c in colors: info[c]=bbox(c),(max(info[c][2]-info[c][0]+1,1)**2+(max(info[c][3]-info[c][1]+1,1)**2))
    inner=min(info,key=lambda c:(info[c][1],))
    mid=[c for c in colors if c!=inner and (info[c][2]-info[c][0]+1)*(info[c][3]-info[c][1]+1)>=(info[inner][2]-info[inner][0]+1)*(info[inner][3]-info[inner][1]+1)][0]
    ri,ci,r2i,c2i=info[inner]; rm,cm,r2m,c2m=info[mid]
    mh=m2= (r2m-rm+1)/2; oh=r2m-rm+1; ow=c2m-cm+1
    ki=(ri+rm)/2; kj=(ci+c2i)/2
    margin=2 if (ri==ri and True) else 2  # placeholder
    inner_is_1x1 = (r2i-ri+1)==1 and (c2i-ci+1)==1
    margin= 1 if inner_is_1x1 else 2
    o=[]
    for i in range(H):
        row=g[i][:]
        for j in range(W):
            v=g[i][j]
            if rm-margin<=i<=r2m+margin and cm-margin<=j<=c2m+margin:
                row[j]= inner if v==bg else v
        o.append(row)
    return o
for n in (1,2,3):
    i=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    p=f(i)
    print(n, p==o)

    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    def bbox(c):
        rs=[i for i,r_ in enumerate(a) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        cs=[j for i,r_ in enumerate(a) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]

    # identify colors by layer: color whose bbox encloses others = frame; smallest = core
    colors=[c for c in cnt if c!=bg]
    boxes={c:bbox(c) for c in colors}
    # ordering by bbox containment: outermost contains all others
    order=[]
    rem=set(colors)
    while rem:
        c=min(rem,key=lambda c:max(b[2]-b[0]+1,b[3]-b[1]+1) for b in [boxes[c]]) if False else None
        rem.discard(next(iter(rem)))

    sorted_cols=sorted(colors,key=lambda c:(bb(boxes[c][2],boxes[c][3])-boxes[c][0]+1)*(boxes[c][3]-boxes[c][1]+1),reverse=True)
    f=sorted_cols[0]; inner=sorted_cols[-1]
    print(n,'frame',f,'core',inner,'bbox frame',boxes[f],'bbox core',boxes[inner])

import json
a=G['Test input']
cnt=collections.Counter(x for r_ in a for x in r_)
bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
colors=[c for c in cnt if c!=bg]
boxes={c:(min(i for i,r_ in enumerate(a) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c),
          min(j for i,r_ in enumerate(a) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c),
          max(i for i,r_ in enumerate(a) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c),
          max(j for i,r_ in enumerate(a) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c)) for c in colors}
areas={c:(b[2]-b[0]+1)*(b[3]-b[1]+1) for c,b in boxes.items()}
f=max(colors,key=lambda c:areas[c]); inner=min(colors,key=lambda c:areas[c])
rf,pi=boxes[f],boxes[inner]
fr=rf[2]-rf[0]+1; fc=pi[2]-pi[0]+1
H,W=len(a),len(a[0])
gr=min(fc,(H-fr)//2); gc=min(fc,(W-(rf[3]-rf[1]+1))//2)
print(f,inner,'gap',gr,gc)
t_r,bb_=rf[0]-gr,rf[2]+gr; l_c,rc2=rf[1]-gc,rf[3]+gc
out=[row[:] for row in a]
for i in range(max(t_r,0),min(bb_,H)):
    for j in range(max(l_c,0),min(rc2,W)):
        if out[i][j]==bg: out[i][j]=inner
print(json.dumps(out))

def solve(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for r_ in g for x in r_)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    colors=[c for c in cnt if c!=bg]
    def bb(c):
        rs=[i for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        cs=[j for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        return min(rs),min(cs),max(rs),max(cs)
    boxes={c:bb(c) for c in colors}
    sizes={c:(b[2]-b[0]+1)*(b[3]-b[1]+1) for c,b in boxes.items()}
    inner=min(sizes,key=sizes.get)
    rf,_=boxes[inner]
    fh,fcw=rf[2]-rf[0]+1,rf[3]-rf[1]+1
    rh,wh=rf[0],rf[1]
    padr=min(fcw,(H-fh)//2); padc=min(rhw if False else 0,0)  # placeholder
    padv=min(fhw if False else 0,0)
    return None

def solve2(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for r_ in g for x in r_)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    colors=[c for c in cnt if c!=bg]
    def bb(c):
        rs=[i for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        cs=[j for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        return min(rs),min(cs),max(rs),max(cs)
    boxes={c:bb(c) for c in colors}
    sizes={c:(b[2]-b[0]+1)*(b[3]-b[1]+1) for c,b in boxes.items()}
    inner=min(sizes,key=sizes.get)
    fr=r_=boxes[inner]
    fh=fr[2]-fr[0]+1; fw=fr[3]-fr[1]+1
    ic=inner
    ph=max(fh,fw)   # core is square here; use its side
    padr=min(ph,(H-fh)//2); padc=min(ph,(W-fw)//2)
    tr=fr[0]-padr; br=fr[2]+padr; lc=fr[1]-padc; rc2=fr[3]+padc
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    for i in range(max(tr,0),min(br+1,H)):
        for j in range(max(lc,0),min(rc2,W)):
            if out[i][j]==bg: out[i][j]=ic
    return out

def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r_.split() for r_ in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r_)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r_) for r_ in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r_] for r_ in rows]
    return G
G=load()
import json,collections
def f(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for r_ in g for x in r_)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    def bb(c):
        rs=[i for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        cs=[j for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
        return min(rs),min(cs),max(rs),max(cs)
    col=[c for c in set(x for r_ in g for x in r_)-{0}]
    boxes={c:bb(c) for c in col}
    sizes={c:(b[2]-b[0]+1)*(b[3]-b[1]+1) for c,b in boxes.items()}
    inner=min(sizes,key=sizes.get); frame=max(sizes,key=lambda k:sizes[k])
    I=boxes[inner]; F=boxes[frame]
    t=max(I[2]-I[0]+1, I[3]-I[1]+1)   # core dimension
    # new block: frame expanded by t each side; centered on frame center
    cy=(F[0]+F[2])/2; cx=(F[1]+F[3])/2
    S=F[2]-F[0]+1+2*t
    br0=int(round(cy-t)); br1=int(round(cy+t))
    bc0=int(round(cx-t)); bc1=int(round(cx+t))
    out=[[bg]*W for _ in range(H)]
    # paint block: outer ring = inner color, inner ring = frame color, core preserved
    rng=[]
    for i in range(S):
        row=[]
        for j in range(S):
            di=i-t; dj=j-t
            # distance layers from center of new block
            dmax=max(abs(i-cy),abs(j-cx))
            if dmax<=t:         # outer ring -> inner color
                row.append(inner)
            elif i>=F[0]-t and i<=F[2]+t and j>=F[1]-t and j<=F[3]+t:
                row.append(frame)
            else:
                row.append(bg)
        rng.append(row)
    # place ring pattern onto grid at correct origin
    for i,row in enumerate(rng):
        for j,v in enumerate(row):
            gi=br0+i; gj=bc0+j
            if 0<=gi<H and 0<=gj<W: out[gi][gj]=v
    # restore original figure (frame & core) — they're inside the inner ring region anyway
    for i in range(F[0],F[2]+1):
        for j in range(F[1],F[3]+1):
            if g[i][j]!=bg: out[i][j]=g[i][j]
    return out
for n in (1,2,3,4):
    a=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; b=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    r_=f(a)
    d=[(i,j,a[i][j],r_[i][j],b[i][j]) for i in range(len(a)) for j in range(len(a[0])) if r_[i][j]!=b[i][j]]
    print(n,'ndiff',len(d), d[:6])
res=f(G['Test input'])
print(json.dumps(res))

import collections
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r_.split() for r_ in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r_)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r_) for r_ in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r_] for r_ in rows]
    return G
G=load()
# For each demo, determine exact padded rectangle dims in OUTPUT (ring bbox incl core)
def box(g,c):
    rs=[i for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
    cs=[j for i,r_ in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(r_) if x==c]
    return min(rs),min(cs),max(rs),max(cs)
for n in (1,2,3,4):
    a=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; b=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    cnt=collections.Counter(x for r_ in a for x in r_)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    col=[c for c in set(x for r_ in a for x in r_)-{bg}]
    def aa(c):
        F_=box(a,c); return (F_[2]-F_[0]+1)*(F_[3]-F_[1]+1)
    fr=max(col,key=lambda k:aa(k)); ic=[c for c in col if c!=fr][0]
    F_=box(a,fr)
    # block rect in out: try candidate rings via which rows contain ic outside fig region... instead: 
    # block dims = dims of largest square block whose border is ic and contains frame? guess from diffs earlier: 
    # use: block height = last row where out has ic before trailing zeros... 
    rows_ic=[i for i in range(len(b)) if any(b[i][j]==ic for j in range(len(b[0])))]
    cols_ic=[j for j in range(len(b[0])) if any(b[i][j]==ic for i in range(len(b)))]
    print(n,'block rows',rows_ic[0],rows_ic[-1],'cols',cols_ic[0],cols_ic[-1],'| frame',(F_[2]-F_[0]+1),(box(a,fr)[3]-box(a,fr)[1]+1),'core',box(a,ic)[2]-box(a,ic)[0]+1)
